comment: Maths MCQ bank, modules 01-04 (4MA1 Higher). Authored from the module content, the 2018 May 1H/2H papers, the 2016 SAMs and the old-spec January papers, with numbers changed. answer = index into options. Distractors are the classic errors (adding indices instead of multiplying, dividing by the new amount, UB - UB for a difference, cancelling terms). Every numerical answer is checked by a script.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is 360 written as a product of powers of its prime factors?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 360 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2³ × 3² × 5. The others multiply to 360 but contain non-primes (10, 45, 60).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the HCF of 2³ × 3² × 5 and 2² × 3⁴ × 7?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: HCF: primes common to both (2 and 3) to their LOWEST powers: 2² × 3² = 36. Taking the highest powers and every prime gives the LCM instead.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 15?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5. LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60. 180 is 12 × 15, a common multiple but not the lowest; 3 is the HCF.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the LCM of 2⁴ × 3 and 2² × 3³ × 5?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: LCM: every prime, highest power: 2⁴, 3³ and 5. Adding the powers (2⁶ × 3⁴) multiplies the numbers together instead; leaving out the 5 misses a prime.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: One light flashes every 8 seconds and another every 12 seconds. They flash together now. After how many seconds do they next flash together?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: The LCM of 8 and 12 is 24. 96 = 8 × 12 is a common multiple but not the first; 4 is the HCF.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is prime?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 51 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19 and 91 = 7 × 13. 59 has no factors other than 1 and itself.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify y⁵ × y⁹
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Multiplying powers of the same base: ADD the indices. 5 + 9 = 14.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify (2m³)⁴
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Everything in the bracket is raised to the power 4: 2⁴ = 16 and (m³)⁴ = m¹². 2m¹² forgets the 2; 16m⁷ adds the indices instead of multiplying.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify (m⁴)⁻³
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Power of a power: multiply the indices. 4 × (−3) = −12.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of c⁰ (c ≠ 0)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: c³ ÷ c³ = c⁰ by the index laws, and anything divided by itself is 1.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write ∛2 as a power of 2
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: A cube root is the power 1/3, because 2^(1/3) × 2^(1/3) × 2^(1/3) = 2¹.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify 12x⁷y² ÷ 4x³y⁵
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Divide the numbers (12 ÷ 4 = 3) and SUBTRACT indices: x⁷⁻³ = x⁴, y²⁻⁵ = y⁻³.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 25^(−1/2)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Negative index → reciprocal; power 1/2 → square root. 1/√25 = 1/5. A negative index never makes the answer negative, and it is not a multiplier (25 × −1/2).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 27^(2/3)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Root first: ∛27 = 3, then square: 3² = 9. 18 comes from 27 × 2/3, which treats the index as a multiplier.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of (16/81)^(−3/4)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Flip for the negative: (81/16)^(3/4). Fourth root: 3/2. Cube: 27/8. 8/27 forgets to flip.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 8^(−2/3)?
9ˣ = 3⁷ × 3. What is the value of x?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Write 9 as 3²: 3²ˣ = 3⁸, so 2x = 8 and x = 4. 8 forgets that 9 is 3².

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: 8 ÷ 2⁷ = 2ⁿ. What is the value of n?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 8 = 2³, so 2³ ÷ 2⁷ = 2³⁻⁷ = 2⁻⁴. n = 4 subtracts the wrong way round.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is √72 written in its simplest form?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Take out the LARGEST square factor: 72 = 36 × 2, so √72 = 6√2. 2√18 and 3√8 are equal to √72 but not fully simplified.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify √48 + √27
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √48 = 4√3 and √27 = 3√3, so the sum is 7√3. √48 + √27 is NOT √75: roots don't add like that (√75 = 5√3).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out √5 × √20
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √5 × √20 = √100 = 10. √25 adds the numbers under the root instead of multiplying them.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Expand and simplify (3 + √5)²
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: (3 + √5)(3 + √5) = 9 + 3√5 + 3√5 + 5 = 14 + 6√5. Just squaring each term (9 + 5) misses the two middle terms.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Expand and simplify (2 + √3)(2 − √3)
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Difference of two squares: 2² − (√3)² = 4 − 3 = 1. The surd terms +2√3 and −2√3 cancel.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Rationalise the denominator of 10/√5
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Multiply top and bottom by √5: 10√5/5 = 2√5.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: To rationalise the denominator of 4/(3 − √5), you multiply the top and bottom by…
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Use the denominator with the sign flipped: (3 − √5)(3 + √5) = 9 − 5 = 4, a whole number. Multiplying by (3 − √5) leaves a surd.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write 4/(3 − √5) in the form a + √b
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 4(3 + √5)/(9 − 5) = 4(3 + √5)/4 = 3 + √5. Dividing by 14 comes from adding 9 + 5 instead of subtracting.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is a surd?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √16 = 4, √0.25 = 0.5 and ∛27 = 3 are all rational. √12 = 2√3 is irrational, so it is a surd.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is irrational?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Recurring decimals and fractions are rational, and √9 = 3. √2 cannot be written as a fraction of integers.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write 0.00052 in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Move the decimal point 4 places to get 5.2, which lies between 1 and 10. The number is small, so the power is negative: 10⁻⁴. 52 × 10⁻⁵ has A bigger than 10.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out (4.2 × 10⁵) × (3 × 10⁻⁸), giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 4.2 × 3 = 12.6 and 10⁵ × 10⁻⁸ = 10⁻³, giving 12.6 × 10⁻³. That is not in standard form, so adjust to 1.26 × 10⁻².

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out (1.2 × 10⁷) ÷ (4.8 × 10³), giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 1.2 ÷ 4.8 = 0.25 and 10⁷ ÷ 10³ = 10⁴, giving 0.25 × 10⁴ = 2.5 × 10³. When A gets 10 times bigger, the power goes DOWN by 1.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out 3.2 × 10⁵ + 4.5 × 10⁴, giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Match the powers: 3.2 × 10⁵ + 0.45 × 10⁵ = 3.65 × 10⁵ (320 000 + 45 000 = 365 000). You cannot add the front numbers when the powers differ.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is written in standard form?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Standard form is A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10 and n an integer. 34 and 0.34 are outside that range, and 0.5 is not an integer.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: A calculator shows 2.52E−03. How should the answer be written?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: E−03 means × 10⁻³. The E notation is not accepted on the answer line, so write it in full.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.4545… (45 recurring)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: x = 0.4545…, 100x = 45.4545…, so 99x = 45 and x = 45/99 = 5/11. 45/100 is 0.45 exactly, which does not recur.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.1444… (4 recurring)?
To write 0.245245… (245 recurring) as a fraction, x is multiplied by which number before subtracting x?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: The repeating block has 3 digits, so use 1000x = 245.245…; then 999x = 245.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.2727… (27 recurring)?
(3 + √x)² = y + 6√2, where x and y are positive integers. Find x and y.
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: (3 + √x)² = 9 + 6√x + x. Matching the surd parts: 6√x = 6√2, so x = 2. Then y = 9 + 2 = 11.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. What is their LCM?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: HCF × LCM = the product of the two numbers, so LCM = 18 × 24 ÷ 6 = 72. 432 is the product itself.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Work out 3 2/5 − 1 3/4
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 17/5 − 7/4 = 68/20 − 35/20 = 33/20 = 1 13/20. Subtracting whole numbers (2) and then fractions needs care: 2/5 − 3/4 is negative (−7/20).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Work out 2 1/3 ÷ 1 5/9
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 7/3 ÷ 14/9 = 7/3 × 9/14 = 63/42 = 3/2. 3 17/27 multiplies by 14/9 without flipping it.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: What single number do you multiply by to increase an amount by 15%?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 100% + 15% = 115% = 1.15. 0.15 gives just the increase; 0.85 is a 15% DEcrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: What single number do you multiply by to decrease an amount by 7.5%?
A price rises from $480 to $552. What is the percentage increase?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Change = 72. 72 ÷ 480 (the ORIGINAL) × 100 = 15%. Dividing by 552 gives 13.0%.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: After a 12% increase a laptop costs $1344. What was the price before the increase?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Original × 1.12 = 1344, so original = 1344 ÷ 1.12 = 1200. Taking 12% off 1344 (× 0.88) gives 1182.72, which is wrong because the 12% was of the original.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: After an 8% pay rise, Mia earns $32 400. What did she earn before the rise?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 32 400 ÷ 1.08 = 30 000. 32 400 × 0.92 = 29 808 takes 8% of the NEW salary, the error that scored M0 M0 A0 in 2018.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: In a 35% sale, a coat costs $91. What was the price before the sale?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Sale price = 65% of the original, so 91 ÷ 0.65 = 140. 91 × 0.65 and 91 × 1.35 apply the percentage to the wrong amount.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A 15% reduction takes $22.50 off the normal price of a mixer. What is the normal price?
$25 000 is invested at 3.5% per year compound interest. What is it worth after 4 years, to the nearest cent?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 25 000 × 1.035⁴ = 28 688.08. $28 500 is SIMPLE interest (3.5% × 4 = 14%). $3688.08 is only the interest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A boat loses 4% of its value each year. Which calculation gives its value after 3 years, starting from V?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Each year multiplies by 0.96, so 3 years is × 0.96³. × 0.88 is simple depreciation (12%); × 0.96 × 3 triples the value.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price rises by 30%, then falls by 20%. What is the overall percentage change?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 1.3 × 0.8 = 1.04, a 4% increase. Percentage changes multiply; they don't add.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price rises by 20%, then the new price falls by 20%. What is the overall change?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so it ends at 96% of the original: a 4% decrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: $2000 is invested at 5% per year compound interest. How much INTEREST is earned in 2 years?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 2000 × 1.05² = 2205, so the interest is 205. $200 is simple interest; $2205 is the total value, not the interest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A car bought for $24 000 depreciates by 12% per year. What is it worth after 2 years?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 24 000 × 0.88² = 18 585.60. $18 240 takes 24% off in one go (simple depreciation).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: $2880 is shared in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7. What is the largest share?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 15 parts, so 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 per part, and 7 × 192 = 1344. $411.43 is 2880 ÷ 7, dividing by a ratio number instead of the total.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Amir and Beth share money in the ratio 5 : 3. Amir gets $36 more than Beth. How much does Beth get?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 parts = $36, so 1 part = $18 and Beth gets 3 × 18 = $54 ($90 is Amir's share).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write the ratio 45 : 60 in its simplest form
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Divide both by the HCF, 15: 3 : 4. 9 : 12 and 15 : 20 are equivalent but not simplest; 4 : 3 is the wrong way round.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write 2.5 × 10³ : 1.5 × 10⁶ in the form 1 : n
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Divide both parts by 2.5 × 10³: 1.5 × 10⁶ ÷ 2.5 × 10³ = 600.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5. What is a : b : c?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Make the b parts equal: 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 and 4 : 5 = 12 : 15, so a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: For the children at a show, girls : boys = 2 : 7. What fraction of the children are girls?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 2 + 7 = 9 parts, of which 2 are girls, so 2/9. 2/7 compares girls to boys, not girls to all children.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is directly proportional to x². y = 45 when x = 3. What is the value of k in y = kx²?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 45 = k × 3² = 9k, so k = 5. 15 comes from using x instead of x².

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y = 5x². What is y when x = 4?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 5 × 4² = 5 × 16 = 80. 400 squares the 5 as well: (5 × 4)².

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: F is inversely proportional to d². F = 20 when d = 3. Which formula is correct?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: F = k/d², so 20 = k/9 and k = 180. 60/d² uses d instead of d² when finding k.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is directly proportional to x³. What happens to y when x is doubled?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: k(2x)³ = 8kx³ = 8y.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is inversely proportional to x². What happens to y when x is tripled?
F is inversely proportional to d². d is increased by 25%. What is the percentage change in F?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: F is multiplied by 1/1.25² = 0.64, which is a 36% decrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Which graph shows that y is directly proportional to x?
options: A straight line crossing the y-axis above the origin
A curve through the origin that gets steeper
A curve that never meets either axis
A straight line through the origin
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: y = kx is a straight line through (0, 0). A line with a y-intercept (y = kx + c) is linear but not proportional. The steepening curve is y ∝ x² and the curve that never meets the axes is y ∝ 1/x.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: 'T is inversely proportional to the square root of L' means…
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Inversely proportional to √L: T = k ÷ √L.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: T = 48/√L. What is T when L = 36?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: √36 = 6, and 48 ÷ 6 = 8. 1.33 is 48 ÷ 36, which forgets the square root.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: £1 = €1.16. What is €348 in pounds?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Euros to pounds: divide by 1.16. 348 ÷ 1.16 = 300. Multiplying gives £403.68, the wrong direction.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: 3/5 of the people in a hall are children. There are 72 children. How many people are in the hall?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 3/5 = 72, so 1/5 = 24 and 5/5 = 120. 43.2 is 3/5 of 72, which works the wrong way.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price falls from $552 to $480. What is the percentage decrease, to 3 significant figures?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Change 72 ÷ ORIGINAL 552 × 100 = 13.0%. 15% divides by the new price.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A trader buys goods for $180 and sells them for $207. What is the percentage profit?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Profit 27 ÷ cost 180 × 100 = 15%.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: x is increased by 8% to give 27 000. Which calculation finds x?
$50 000 is invested at 3% per year compound interest. What is it worth after 2 years?
Dividing by 14/9 is the same as multiplying by…
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its reciprocal, because 14/9 × 9/14 = 1.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write 36 as a fraction of 60, in its simplest form
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 36/60: divide top and bottom by 12 to get 3/5. 36/60 is right but not simplest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Which of these does NOT show y directly proportional to x?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Proportional means y = kx with no added constant. y = 2x + 3 does not double when x doubles.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Raj earns $20 000 and gets a 10% rise. Sam earns $17 600. What percentage rise must Sam get to earn the same as Raj?

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 7.2968 to 2 decimal places
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The third decimal is 6, so 7.29 rounds up to 7.30. Keep the trailing zero: it shows the accuracy is 2 dp.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 0.004076 to 2 significant figures
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The first significant figure is the 4. Keep 4 and 0; the next digit is 7, so round up to 0.0041.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 38 472 to 3 significant figures
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Keep 3, 8, 4; the next digit is 7, so round up to 385, then fill with zeros to keep the size: 38 500.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: How many significant figures does 0.04070 have?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Count from the first non-zero digit: 4, 0, 7, 0. The zero between 4 and 7 counts, and the final zero shows the accuracy.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 0.0060749 to 2 decimal places
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The second decimal place is 0 and the next digit is 6, so round up to 0.01. 0.0061 is 2 SIGNIFICANT figures, not 2 dp.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Estimate (48.7 × 3.12) ÷ 0.487 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: (50 × 3) ÷ 0.5 = 150 ÷ 0.5 = 300. Dividing by 0.5 DOUBLES. The exact value is 312.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length is 6.4 cm correct to 1 decimal place. What is its upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Half of 0.1 is 0.05, so the bounds are 6.35 and 6.45. The upper bound is written 6.45, not 6.49.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length l is 7.4 cm correct to 1 decimal place. Which is the error interval?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The lower bound 7.35 is included (it rounds up to 7.4) and the upper bound 7.45 is not (it would round to 7.5).

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: 3400 g is correct to 2 significant figures. What is the lower bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The second significant figure is in the hundreds, so it was rounded to the nearest 100. Half of 100 is 50: 3400 − 50 = 3350.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A mass is 70 kg to the nearest 5 kg. What are its bounds?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Half of 5 is 2.5, so 70 ± 2.5.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The distance from A to B is 110 km correct to 2 significant figures. What is the upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 2 sf, 110 is rounded to the nearest 10. Half of 10 is 5, so the upper bound is 115.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: There are 1300 sheets correct to the nearest 100. What is the lower bound?
a = 8.3 and b = 5.6, both to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of a × b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: For a product, the maximum is UB × UB: 8.35 × 5.65 = 47.1775.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: a = 12.4 and b = 5.7, both to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of a − b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Largest a minus SMALLEST b: 12.45 − 5.65 = 6.8. UB − UB gives 6.7, which is not the maximum.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: a = 12.4 and b = 5.7, both to 1 dp. What is the lower bound of a − b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Smallest a minus LARGEST b: 12.35 − 5.75 = 6.6.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: e = 6.47 and f = 2.83, both to 2 dp. What is the upper bound of e − f?
Which gives the upper bound of a speed, where speed = distance ÷ time?
options: UB of distance ÷ UB of time
LB of distance ÷ LB of time
UB of distance ÷ LB of time
LB of distance ÷ UB of time
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: A fraction is largest with the biggest top and the smallest bottom. LB ÷ UB gives the LOWER bound.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A runner covers 200 m (nearest 5 m) in 24.6 s (nearest 0.1 s). What is the upper bound of the speed, to 3 sf?
1300 sheets (nearest 100) make a pile 160 mm high (nearest 10 mm). Which calculation gives the UPPER bound of the thickness of one sheet?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Thickness = height ÷ number. For the maximum: largest height ÷ smallest number = 165 ÷ 1250 = 0.132 mm.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = (a + b)/c with a = 5.3, b = 2.1 and c = 1.8, all to 1 dp. Which gives the upper bound of y?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Make the top as big as possible and the bottom as small as possible.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = 3a/(b − c). For the LARGEST y, which bounds of b and c should you use?
options: Lower bound of b and upper bound of c
Upper bound of b and lower bound of c
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To make y big, the denominator b − c must be SMALL: small b minus big c.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = 3a/(b − c) with a = 42, b = 31, c = 17, each to 2 sf. What is the lower bound of y, to 2 sf?
A rectangle is 20 cm by 11 cm, each to the nearest cm. What is the smallest possible area as a percentage of the largest, to 3 sf?
The side of a cube is 6.2 cm to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of its volume?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Use the upper bound of the side, 6.25, and cube it: 244.14… cm³.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A circle has area 50 cm² to the nearest cm². What is the lower bound of its radius, to 3 sf?
P = 23.7 × 8.46 (23.7 to 1 dp, 8.46 to 2 dp). The bounds of P are 199.96… and 201.04… To what accuracy can P be given?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 3 sf the bounds give 200 and 201, which disagree. To 2 sf both give 200, so P = 200 to 2 sf.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: z = x/y with bounds 13.478 (upper) and 13.423 (lower). What is z to a suitable degree of accuracy?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 3 sf the bounds round to 13.5 and 13.4, which disagree. To 2 sf both round to 13.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: An angle is 38° correct to 2 significant figures. What is its lower bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 2 sf, 38 is rounded to the nearest 1. Half of 1 is 0.5, so the lower bound is 37.5°.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The volume of a sphere of radius 2.35 cm is 54.36… cm³. What goes wrong if you round the radius to 2.4 first?
options: You get about 57.9 cm³, which is too big
Nothing: the answer still rounds to 54.4
You get about 54.9 cm³, which is slightly too big
You get about 52.0 cm³, which is too small
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 4/3 × π × 2.4³ = 57.9. Cubing magnifies the rounding error, so keep full values and round once at the end.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: 100 eggs are packed in boxes of 12. How many boxes are needed to hold all of them?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 100 ÷ 12 = 8.33… Eight boxes hold only 96 eggs, so round UP to 9 boxes.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length is 5.8 cm correct to 2 significant figures. What is the upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 2 sf for 5.8 means to 1 dp. Half of 0.1 is 0.05, so the upper bound is 5.85.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The time taken for a journey is 150 km (2 sf) ÷ 60 km/h (nearest 5 km/h). Which gives the LOWER bound of the time?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Time = distance ÷ speed. The minimum is the smallest distance ÷ the largest speed = 145 ÷ 62.5 = 2.32 h.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Mass 440 g (nearest 10 g), volume 52 cm³ (nearest cm³). What is the upper bound of the density, to 3 sf?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 445 ÷ 51.5 = 8.640… → 8.64. Density is a division, so use UB mass ÷ LB volume.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A hypotenuse is 12 cm (nearest cm) and an angle is 40° (nearest degree). What is the upper bound of the opposite side, 12 sin 40°?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: sin increases between 0° and 90°, so the largest value uses the largest angle and the largest hypotenuse: 12.5 × sin 40.5° = 8.12 cm.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Which is the correct way to give a final answer of 28 688.075… dollars?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Money is given to 2 dp (the nearest cent). The third decimal is 5, so round up to .08.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The perimeter of a rectangle 8.3 cm by 5.6 cm (each to 1 dp) has what upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 2 × (8.35 + 5.65) = 2 × 14 = 28. For a sum, use both upper bounds.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: x = 7.3 and y = 2.1, both to 1 dp. Which gives the LOWER bound of x ÷ y?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: For the smallest quotient, divide the smallest top by the largest bottom.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A value is 2.4 to 1 dp. Why is 2.45 used as its upper bound, even though 2.45 rounds to 2.5?
options: Because 2.45 is closer to 2.4 than to 2.5
Because upper bounds are always rounded down
It isn't: the upper bound is 2.449
The value can be anything up to, but not including, 2.45
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The true value can get as close to 2.45 as you like, so 2.45 is the boundary: 2.35 ≤ x < 2.45.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: With no instruction about accuracy, how should a non-exact decimal answer normally be given?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Edexcel expects 3 sf unless told otherwise (angles to 1 dp). Write the longer value first, then the rounded one.

04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: (3x − 2)(3x − 2) = 9x² − 6x − 6x + 4. Squaring each term misses the two middle terms.
(x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − x − 6; × (x + 4) gives x³ + 4x² − x² − 4x − 6x − 24 = x³ + 3x² − 10x − 24. The constant is 2 × −3 × 4 = −24.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: When (x + 5)(x − 3)(x + 3) is expanded, what is the constant term?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: The constant comes only from 5 × (−3) × 3 = −45.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: How many terms are there after multiplying a simplified quadratic (3 terms) by a bracket with 2 terms, before collecting?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 3 × 2 = 6 terms. Expanding all three brackets at once gives 8 terms. The 2018 scheme required the correct number of terms to be present.
HCF of 15 and 25 is 5, and the lowest powers are a² and b. The other answers still have a common factor left in the bracket.
HCF(24, 36) = 12; lowest powers a² and b². What is left is 2a − 3b².
The two numbers must multiply to −30 and add to +1: 6 and −5. (x − 6)(x + 5) gives −x.
Multiply to −40, add to −3: −8 and +5.
ac = −72; 9 and −8 multiply to −72 and add to 1. So 6x² + 9x − 8x − 12 = 3x(2x + 3) − 4(2x + 3).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: In the ac method for 6x² + x − 12, which two numbers do you look for?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Multiply a × c = 6 × −12 = −72, and the sum must be b = 1.
Difference of two squares: (5x)² − (6y)² = (5x − 6y)(5x + 6y).
Take out the common factor 2 first, then factorise the difference of squares: x² − 25 = (x − 5)(x + 5). 2(x² − 25) is not completely factorised.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Which of these can NOT be factorised using real numbers?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: x² + 9 is a SUM of squares. x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), 9 − x² = (3 − x)(3 + x), and x² − 9x = x(x − 9).
3x(x − 2) / ((x − 2)(x + 2)). Cancel the common FACTOR (x − 2).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: A student writes (x + 3)/(x + 5) = 3/5. What is wrong?
options: x is a term, not a factor, so it cannot be cancelled
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: You can only cancel factors. Test x = 1: 4/6 = 2/3, which is not 3/5.
[2(x − 1) + 5(x + 3)] / ((x + 3)(x − 1)) = (2x − 2 + 5x + 15)/… = (7x + 13)/((x + 3)(x − 1)). You cannot add the tops and bottoms separately.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: What is the simplest common denominator for 1/(9x² − 25) − 1/(6x + 10)?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 9x² − 25 = (3x − 5)(3x + 5) and 6x + 10 = 2(3x + 5). The LCM uses each factor once: 2(3x − 5)(3x + 5).
Common denominator 2(2x − 3)(2x + 3). Numerator 2 − (2x − 3) = 5 − 2x. The minus sign must go through the whole bracket.
Flip and multiply, then factorise: (x − 4)(x + 4)/[3(x + 4)] × 6x/[(x − 4)(x + 1)] = 2x/(x + 1).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make p the subject of N = pq − rs
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Add rs to both sides: pq = N + rs, then divide by q. Write p = at the start. The 2018 scheme only gave the A1 if the answer was seen with the subject and an equals sign.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make r the subject of V = πr²h/3
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 3V = πr²h, so r² = 3V/(πh) and r = √(3V/(πh)). Stopping at r² does not make r the subject.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make L the subject of T = 2π√(L/g)
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: T/(2π) = √(L/g), square: T²/(4π²) = L/g, then multiply by g.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make v the subject of E = ½mv² + h, where v is positive
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: E − h = ½mv², so v² = 2(E − h)/m, then take the positive square root.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make q the subject of p = (2q + 1)/(q − 3)
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: pq − 3p = 2q + 1 → pq − 2q = 1 + 3p → q(p − 2) = 1 + 3p. The first wrong answer still has q on both sides.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: When the subject appears in two terms, which step MUST you use?
options: Divide both sides by the subject
Cancel the subject from both sides
Factorise the subject out of the terms that contain it
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Collect the subject terms on one side, then factorise, e.g. q(p − 2) = 1 + 3p, so you can divide by the bracket.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make a the subject of 2a − 7 = (5 + a)/k

04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Collect the g terms: 5g − 4eg = 3 − 2e, then factorise: g(5 − 4e) = 3 − 2e.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make y the subject of x = √((y + 2)/(y − 1))
Which expression represents any odd number, where n is an integer?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 2n is always even, so 2n + 1 is always odd. n + 1 and n² can be either odd or even.
4n² + 12n + 9 − (4n² + 4n + 1) = 8n + 8 = 8(n + 1), a multiple of 8.
(4n² + 12n + 9) − (4n² − 12n + 9) = 24n = 12 × 2n, so it is always a multiple of 12.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Why is 'it works for n = 1, 2 and 3' not a proof?
options: Examples only check some cases; a proof must work for every n
Three examples are not enough, but ten would be
It is a proof if the examples are chosen at random
It is a proof if n = 0 is also checked
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: However many examples you try, you have not covered every integer. Algebra with a general n does.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: The sum of three consecutive integers n, n + 1 and n + 2 is always…
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), a multiple of 3. It can be odd or even (e.g. 6 and 9).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Which is an identity (true for ALL values of x)?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: An identity holds for every x. x² = 4 and 2x + 1 = 7 are equations; (x + 1)² = x² + 1 is false for most x.
